title: Terminal and Signal
premise: Jude Sandoval, a terraformer ferrying seed-stock between two colonies that severed contact decades ago, discovers their own name on the manifest of a ship that never launched—a vessel carrying half a million cryosleepers from the dead world of Meridian. The manifest is a message from Jude's former lover, Wren, who now administers the sleepers and has secretly scheduled only one colony's bloodline to wake. As Jude races between worlds running the long route no one else will fly, they must choose: expose Wren's rigged lottery and doom both colonies to slow attrition, or let it stand and betray everyone they've ever tended. In the end, Jude broadcasts the true manifest to both worlds, waking all the sleepers in shifts neither government authorized, and loses Wren to the consequences—but keeps the garden alive for people who will actually arrive.
about_author: Gideon Underhill is the pen name of a former hydrologist who spent six years on remote research stations before turning to fiction. They write quiet, rigorous science fiction about people who maintain things—gardens, ships, promises.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Establishes the solo run between colonies Vespera and Calloway, tending the orbital seed-garden meant for future generations. The emotional beat is lonely competence—Jude has made peace with being unnecessary to the living.

chapters.title: Manifest Anomaly
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. A routine cargo audit surfaces a ship that never flew—the Meridian—and Jude Sandoval listed as passenger 4,417. Fear creeps under the routine; someone knows who Jude was before the garden.

chapters.title: What Meridian Was
chapters.summary: Jude's POV, with flashback fragments. We learn Meridian died in the Severance, its half-million citizens frozen mid-evacuation, and that Jude fled it years ago. The beat is dread: the past has found a shipping lane.

chapters.title: Wren
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. A delayed transmission arrives from Wren Ashari, Jude's former lover, now Chief Steward of the cryo-vaults—signed to the ghost manifest. Old love and old betrayal surface together; Jude answers against every instinct for safety.

chapters.title: Calloway Side of Silence
chapters.summary: Callum Reyes, a Calloway dock clerk, POV. He notices Jude's ship querying restricted vault frequencies and files it away. The beat is institutional suspicion—the machinery of both worlds beginning to turn toward Jude.

chapters.title: The Lottery That Isn't
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. We see her secret: the wake schedule prioritizes Vesperan genomes, written off as 'genetic triage.' She believes she is saving humanity from itself. Her conviction is chillingly sincere.

chapters.title: Garden Logic
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Tending the seed-garden, Jude works through what the manifest means: Wren wants them as witness or hostage. The beat is a lover's argument conducted in botany metaphors—what deserves to grow, and who decides.

chapters.title: Interception
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. Calloway authorities detain Jude's ship on arrival, having decoded the vault queries. Interrogation reveals how much both governments fear the Meridian sleepers—as labor, as leverage, as plague.

chapters.title: Two Worlds, No Words
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Released but shadowed, Jude learns the colonies' silence is mutual embargo, each blaming the other for Meridian. The beat is bitter clarity: the sleepers are hostages in a war nobody admits is happening.

chapters.title: Wren's Confession
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, long letter-chapter. She explains the schedule, the manifest, and asks Jude to run one last route: deliver the wake keys to Vespera before Calloway can seize them. She frames it as mercy. It reads like a dare.

chapters.title: The Copy
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude duplicates the full manifest and wake schedule, intending blackmail leverage, then hesitates—exposure means both governments seize the vaults and the sleepers never wake at all. The beat is moral vertigo.

chapters.title: Running Dark
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude flies the route with transponders cold, hunted by both colonies, carrying the keys. A near-miss with a Calloway patrol costs them the seed-garden's uplink. Isolation deepens; the garden goes silent behind them.

chapters.title: Hostage Garden
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. Calloway impounds the seed-garden as collateral, and Callum—sympathetic, methodical—realizes the sleepers are the only thing keeping either world from open war. He begins his own quiet investigation into the schedule.

chapters.title: Vespera
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Arrival at Vespera, where Wren waits in person for the first time in nine years. The reunion is tender and ruinous: they still love each other, and it changes nothing about what each will do. The beat is love against duty, fully armed.

chapters.title: The Argument in the Vault Antechamber
chapters.summary: Alternating Jude/Wren. Face to face among the sleepers, they argue the book's central question: is a rigged rescue better than an honest catastrophe? Neither concedes. Wren initiates the wake sequence anyway, starting with Vesperans.

chapters.title: Seizure
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. Calloway fleet jumps to Vespera, tipped by Callum's own report—his justice has become a weapon. The beat is guilt: he wanted accountability and may have triggered a war over sleeping bodies.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Jude's POV, climax begins. With fleets inbound and the sequence running, Jude makes the choice: broadcast the true manifest, the rigged schedule, and the wake keys openly to both worlds—no secrets left to fight over. Wren tries to stop them; Jude doesn't fight back.

chapters.title: What Wren Did
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Rather than let Calloway seize the vaults, Wren diverts vault power to shield Jude's broadcast, burning her authority and, implicitly, herself. Her last act as Steward is to unlock everything. The beat is sacrifice as answer.

chapters.title: Standoff at the Vaults
chapters.summary: Callum's POV, climax resolves. Both fleets hold position over unlocked vaults they cannot claim without admitting the embargo's lies. Callum proposes the unthinkable aloud: joint stewardship, shared wakes. Exhaustion does what courage couldn't.

chapters.title: Shifts
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The accord: all sleepers wake in mixed-colony shifts over thirty years, administered by a council including Callum. Justice outside the law, barely. The first sleepers open their eyes to a garden signal Jude restored.

chapters.title: Sentencing
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren surrenders to the joint council; her sentence is service—she will tend the wake-shifts she rigged, under supervision. Jude visits once. Forgiveness is not offered, but neither is hatred. Some doors stay ajar.

chapters.title: People Not Yet Born
chapters.summary: Jude's POV, coda. Years later, Jude runs the route again, garden replanted, first wakers walking its rows. The final beat is earned hope: the garden was always for people not yet born, and now, finally, some of them have arrived.
